title: Noise, interference and grounding
blurb: Identify noise sources by their signature, choose blankers, notch filters and chokes, and place surge protectors on a single point ground.

E4E01.why: An ANF removes steady tones, and a **CW signal is a steady tone** too, so it removes the **CW signal as well**.
E4E01.trap: Ringing and overload aren't the ANF's CW problem.

E4E02.why: DSP noise reduction can reduce **white noise, ignition noise and power line noise**: all of them.

E4E03.why: A blanker mutes the receiver during short pulses, so it removes **impulse noise**.
E4E03.trap: Hum, buzz and steady white noise aren't pulses.

E4E04.why: Alternator noise travels on the charging leads. **Ferrite chokes on those leads** suppress it.
E4E04.trap: Capacitors in series would block the charging current, not the noise.

E4E05.why: A **brute-force AC-line filter in series** with the motor's power leads keeps its noise off the line.
E4E05.trap: A high-pass filter would also block the 60 Hz power.

E4E06.why: Network gear radiates **unstable modulated or unmodulated signals at specific frequencies**.
E4E06.trap: Hum, clicks and pulsing whines are other sources' signatures.

E4E07.why: **Common-mode currents** on the shield and conductors turn a shielded cable into an antenna.
E4E07.trap: Low-inductance grounds and braided shield are good practice, not the cause.

E4E08.why: Current that flows **equally on all conductors** is **common-mode** current. Differential current flows in opposite directions.

E4E09.why: Strong signals can trigger a blanker, which **distorts them and can seem to cause spurious emissions**.
E4E09.trap: Blankers don't narrow audio or break FM demodulation.

E4E10.why: Arcing thermostats, defective doorbell transformers and faulty signs all cause intermittent roaring or buzzing: **all of these**.

E4E11.why: **Corroded metal connections** act like diodes, mix the broadcast signals and reradiate the products.
E4E11.trap: Receiver overload would be inside your radio, not in nearby metal.

E4E12.why: A switch-mode supply's switching harmonics show up as **carriers at regular intervals** across a wide range.
E4E12.trap: Radar, cameras and electric fences produce other patterns.

E4E13.why: Mount the AC surge protector **on the single point ground panel** so it shares the same ground as every other protector.
E4E13.trap: The AC panel or outlet gives it a different ground from the rest.

E4E14.why: One panel, one ground: **all lightning protectors activate together**, so no cable sits at a different potential.
